title: The Department's published follow-up position for oral prescriptions issued under an ePrescribing exception
subtopic: Oral prescription follow-up in Department guidance
rule_summary: DPH Circular DCP 19-12-108, the Electronic Prescribing and Dispensing Manual dated 12/27/2019, states that when an exception applies prescribers may issue written or oral prescriptions, which may be dispensed by pharmacists as valid prescriptions provided the prescription meets the format and security requirements outlined in regulation. It states that IF AN ORAL PRESCRIPTION IS ISSUED FOR A CONTROLLED SUBSTANCE IN SCHEDULE II-V UNDER ONE OF THE EXCEPTIONS, state law requires the prescriber to issue a WRITTEN OR ELECTRONIC follow-up prescription to the dispensing pharmacy WITHIN SEVEN BUSINESS DAYS; that the follow-up prescription must include on its face a notation that the prescription is being issued to document an oral prescription; that a written follow-up may be delivered to the pharmacy in person or by mail and, if mailed, must be postmarked within the seven business day timeframe; and that NO WRITTEN FOLLOW-UP IS REQUIRED FOR SCHEDULE VI ORAL PRESCRIPTIONS. It states that, as with the other exceptions, an oral prescription for a controlled substance in Federal schedule II-V issued in an EMERGENCY SITUATION must be followed within seven business days by a written or electronic prescription for the emergency quantity, including the notation Issued to Document an Oral Prescription; that when an oral prescription for a schedule II controlled substance is issued in an emergency situation the follow-up written or electronic prescription must include the ADDITIONAL NOTATION Authorization for Emergency Dispensing; and that if a prescriber fails to issue a follow-up written or electronic prescription within seven business days, the pharmacist is required to notify the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration of that failure.
exam_relevance: Tests the Department's stated position on the follow-up: every oral schedule II-V prescription issued under an ePrescribing exception, the emergency included, is followed within seven business days by a written or electronic prescription carrying the oral-prescription notation, with Authorization for Emergency Dispensing added for an emergency schedule II prescription.

authority.name: DCP Electronic Prescribing and Dispensing Manual
authority.section: DCP 19-12-108; Written or Electronic Follow-Up Prescription; Emergency Situations; Emergency Prescribing of Schedule II Controlled Substances

numeric_facts.fact: Follow-up to an oral schedule II-V prescription issued under an ePrescribing exception, as the Department states it
numeric_facts.conditions: Written or electronic; a mailed written follow-up must be postmarked within the timeframe; no written follow-up is required for schedule VI

exceptions: The Manual states that no written follow-up is required for schedule VI oral prescriptions.
For an emergency schedule II oral prescription the Manual adds the Authorization for Emergency Dispensing notation and points to additional federal follow-up requirements.
common_confusions: Treating the Department's seven business days as the same count as the 7 days stated in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(c).

Dropping the oral-prescription notation from an emergency schedule II follow-up because it already carries Authorization for Emergency Dispensing, which the Manual describes as an additional notation.
